races.title: State Senate, District 40
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Bobbie Shields
cands.bio: Licensed civil engineer and small business owner who graduated from NC State in 1975 and earned an MBA from UNC-Charlotte. He says he served as interim Mecklenburg County Manager and interim assessor. Republican nominee for NC Senate District 40 in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2026.

endorsements.text: The Charlotte Observer Editorial Board is listed as endorsing his 2026 campaign.

cands.gaps: We could not confirm Shields's birthplace, hometown or when he came to North Carolina. His own description as a lifetime resident is the only evidence. We found no documented deeds or specific stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or foreign land buyers, growth and land protection, guns, abortion, police pay or school choice. His site lists downloadable PDFs on immigration, leadership and racism that could not be read, so we cannot report his immigration position. His general statements about supporting teachers and attracting jobs were too vague to match to any specific policy. His career details, including the interim county manager and assessor roles, come from his own campaign site and survey answers. We found no independent reporting or official records confirming them. We found no controversies, foreign ties or land-use statements.

local.label: Roots 90: In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey he described himself as a lifetime resident of North Carolina, but no source gives his birthplace or hometown.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Civil engineer and small business owner. By his own account he spent about half his career in county government in Mecklenburg County, where he was interim County Manager and interim Assessor, managed the Capital Improvement Program, and administered subdivision and land development ordinances. He worked eleven years in the electrical power industry and has taught engineering technology at UNC-Charlotte.
qual.why: He has executive experience in local government, an engineering career and business ownership, which puts him in the middle range. He has no legislative service and no elected office that the sources confirm. The career details come from his own campaign site and survey answers.

cands.name: Joyce Waddell
cands.bio: Democrat who has served in the North Carolina Senate for District 40 since January 2015. Earlier she served on the Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools Board of Education (District 3). She has three decades in education, including 21 years as a teacher and administrator in Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools.

endorsements.text: For 2026, Ballotpedia lists voter-guide recommendations from several Sway voting groups, including NC Public School Champions and "Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress" (Vote for Peace). These are guides on the Sway platform, not organizational endorsements.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Waddell grew up or when she moved to North Carolina; the only birthplace information is that she is a native of Mullins, South Carolina. The sponsored-bills list on her page was empty, so we could not document bills she authored. We found no documented stances or actions from her on data centers, development and growth, homestead property taxes, out-of-state or investor land buying, immigration and H-1B, policing, gun laws, or abortion. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys for 2020 through 2026, and her only recorded statements are the 2018 survey answers on the minimum wage, Medicaid expansion and public school funding. We found no controversies, foreign ties or notable organizational endorsements in the pages available.

local.label: Roots 55: She is a Mullins, SC native, and the record shows more than 30 years in North Carolina as an adult: 21 years in Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools, a school board seat, and Senate service since 2015. The date she arrived and where she grew up are not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator since 2015 (11 years). Before that she was a Charlotte-Mecklenburg school board member (elected unopposed in 2013) and spent 21 years as a teacher and administrator in Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools, within about three decades in education. She holds a Ph.D. in education-related study from UNC Greensboro.
qual.why: Over a decade of prior legislative service, plus local elected office and a long career in public education administration, fits the high band for writing law and the state budget. Committee seats were not counted.
